newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS - Ambroveneto 1996 net profit rises.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Ambroveneto 1996 net profit rises.

text.p: One of Italy's largest banks Banco Ambrosiano Veneto on Tuesday reported a 6.5 percent rise in 1996 net profits at the parent company levels boosted by increased income from the bank's fund and asset managment operations.

The bank said in a statement that it had held its 1996 dividend on ordinary shares steady at 160 lire/share and on savings shares at 180 lire/share, while net profits were 171 billion lire ($103 million) after 1995's 160 billion lire.

Analysts said the 1996 results were generally in line with expectations and pointed towards a consolidated group net profit up five percent at 190 billion lire and adjusted for extraordinary items up 12 percent at 205 billion lire.
The group said its consolidated 1996 results when published would show a return on equity of over eight percent.

Bank net interest income in 1996 rose five percent to 1.597 trillion lire -- the difference between income interest received from loans and that paid out to depositers -- but growth was greater in some other areas.

It pointed out that growth in commissions relating to mutual funds rose 56.5 percent, that to equity management was up 18.3 percent, life insurance policies up 13.8 percent while placement of credit cards showed a 40.7 percent increase.
The bank said operating costs had increased 5.1 percent due largely to the effect of rises in new work contracts and costs involved with the expansion of the bank's commercial network.
It did not make any comment on the formal approach made earlier this month by Italy's largest savings bank Cariplo about a strategic alliance which might lead to a full merger.
Analysts said that this would create Italy's largest banking group and more significantly the largest bank in Italy's northern industrial heartland of Lombardia and Veneto.
Ambroveneto shares ended up 1.32 percent at 4,290 lire in a slightly firmer Milan stock market.
